hook: An agent that validates forecast files end-to-end — hours of line-by-line comparison down to minutes.

problem.statementExec: Every planning cycle, two families of forecast spreadsheets have to agree. Today, analysts open them side by side and hunt mismatches by hand — hundreds of rows, many sheets, dozens of quarterly periods.
problem.statementTech: Baseline planning files and integration plan files must reconcile across multiple business modules, each with its own file layout, sheet conventions and quirks. The comparison is manual, error-prone, inconsistent between teams, and unscalable as forecast cycles multiply.
painPoints: Several hours of analyst time per validation
The human eye silently misses mismatches
Every module demanded its own manual procedure
marginNotes: 8+ module variants · one specialised skill each

approach.summaryExec: We built an agentic platform that runs the whole validation on its own — it reads the files, works out how they map to each other, compares them to the last decimal, and hands back a colour-coded workbook and a summary.

stages.label: Route
stages.captionExec: The system recognises which business module a file belongs to and picks the right specialist.
stages.captionTech: Keyword-based skill router dispatches to a module-specific sub-agent with its own rules, logic and alias configuration.

stages.label: Explore
stages.captionExec: The agent opens both files and learns their structure — nothing is hard-coded.
stages.captionTech: The agent writes and runs throwaway inspection scripts: header rows, sheet names, period labels, wide-format pivots, scale factors.

stages.label: Plan
stages.captionExec: It reasons about how the two files correspond before comparing anything.
stages.captionTech: Multi-step reasoning over column mappings, key columns, period normalisation and unit scaling, adapted per file pair.

stages.label: Compare
stages.captionExec: A full, precise comparison runs — down to the tenth decimal place.
stages.captionTech: The agent generates pandas/openpyxl comparison code, executes it, and produces a colour-coded result workbook.

stages.label: Verify
stages.captionExec: The agent checks its own output before calling the job done.
stages.captionTech: Self-verification reads the generated workbook back and confirms completeness before reporting.

stages.label: Report
stages.captionExec: You get the workbook plus a written summary — and nothing else is left behind.
stages.captionTech: Summary generated strictly from the output file; temporary scripts and intermediates are cleaned up automatically.

engine.evaluation: Each module skill was validated against known-good manual comparisons across 8+ module variants, with mismatches verified at cell level. Every job is logged with full timestamps and agent execution traces, so any result can be replayed and audited.

value.before: Analysts spent hours per validation, errors slipped through, output format depended on who ran the check, and each new module meant writing a new manual procedure.
value.after: A single submission runs the whole validation autonomously: cell-level precision, a standardised colour-coded workbook, a written summary, and coverage of every module variant through specialised skills.

metrics.label: module variants handled by specialised skills
manual scripting needed per new cycle

roi.formula: hours = validations * mins / 60 * 4.33; value = hours * rate
roi.footnote: Illustrative estimate based on outcomes observed in comparable engagements. Not a quote.
